To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

optical bistability can be used to construct purely optical logic elements that are the basic building blocks of optical computers, and that these logic elements can be constructed using vacuum-deposited thin films.
optical bistability in thin-film interferometer devices is a robust effect, and that it can be used to construct a variety of discrete optical logic elements.

the following purely optical devices were realized: (a) a logic element with a threshold response to the input signal, which can be used as a logic element or an optically programmed component in optical data processing systems, and (b) a relaxation oscillator with a threshold response that can be used as an optical timer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of optical bistability in thin films to optical computing and to optical signal processing.

the development of a new class of bistable devices based on optical interference in thin films, and with the application of these devices to the construction of optically programmed discrete logic elements.
the construction and operation of purely optical discrete logic elements and with the design of optical computer systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
optical logic elements based on thin-film interferometer optical bistable devices are a practical reality.
the optical logic elements described here are not only feasible but that they can be made to work reliably and reproducibly.
the present state of the art of optical bistability is such that it is now possible to build a purely optical computer with a large capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a wide variety of discrete logic elements based upon optical bistability in thin-film interferometric devices.
the optical logic elements are very fast, but the switching time is limited by the speed of the laser pulse, which is not yet fast enough for the realization of an optical computer.
we have demonstrated a variety of purely optical discrete logic elements, and we have shown the feasibility of using these elements in an optical processor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical bistability in thin-film interferometer is not only a phenomenon but also a useful device for the construction of optical computing devices.
it is possible to construct purely optical logic elements based on optical bistability in thin-film interferometer structures with intermediate ZnSe or ZnS layers.
it is possible to construct purely optical discrete logic elements that are capable of processing information in a manner analogous to that used in conventional electronic digital computers.
